description: Verify that DUT uses randomized exponential backoff for DHCPDISCOVER retransmissions: first interval = 4 ± 1 s, second = 8 ± 1 s (RFC 2131 §4.1 SHOULD)
approach:
[Objective]
The SHOULD-randomization on top of RFC 2131 §4.1 doubling: each retx interval gets a small random jitter (typically ±1 s). The first should be in [3, 5] s, second in [7, 9] s. Without jitter, simultaneously-booting clients sync up and stampede the server.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester silent: no OFFER ever sent.
2. DUT → wire: DISCOVER #1, #2, #3.
   • Δt(#2-#1) ∈ [3, 5] s   ← key check 1
   • Δt(#3-#2) ∈ [7, 9] s   ← key check 2

[Pass condition]
First and second retx intervals fall inside the randomized exponential bounds.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_no_discover_<k> — DISCOVER #k missing
• Fail_first_interval_out_of_range — first retx outside [3, 5] s
• Fail_second_interval_out_of_range — second retx outside [7, 9] s

verdicts.Pass: DUT retx intervals match randomized exponential pattern — normal
verdicts.Fail_no_discover: No DUT DHCPDISCOVER within the listen window
verdicts.Fail_first_interval_out_of_range: DUT first retx interval out of [3, 5] s
verdicts.Fail_second_interval_out_of_range: DUT second retx interval out of [7, 9] s
